<objective>
Close BLOCKER 2: a transient fault de-enrols the tablet. `exitOwnerUnlock` reads
`venue_devices` with `const { data: device } = await supabase...maybeSingle()` and discards the
error, so `device` is null for two different facts — no live registry row, which is terminal,
and the query failed, which is not. Both funnel into the outcome `device-not-active`, which
`lib/device-cookie-policy.ts` correctly treats as terminal and answers with deletes for BOTH
cookies. The policy module is right; the caller hands it a fact it never observed, so the
module's seven tests cannot see the defect.

**As a** restaurant owner whose Supabase connection blipped for two minutes during Saturday
service, **I want to** find every tablet still enrolled when it comes back,
**so that** I am not walking the floor re-enrolling devices by hand while the room is full.

Purpose: `IdleRelock` re-enters this path every three idle minutes on any owner-unlocked
tablet, so a few minutes of interruption de-enrols every owner-unlocked tablet in the estate,
each needing someone on site to sign in as the owner and re-run `/enable-staff-mode`. That
inverts the rule the policy module's own header states — cleared only when the browser is
provably no longer this tablet, "and never for a failure that is merely transient" — and
contradicts `lib/venue-authority.ts`, which refuses this exact conflation one file over, in
code written during the same closure run.

Output: the read fault becomes a fact with its own name, the caller stops throwing the error
channel away, `actions/devices.ts` is executed by the suite for the first time, and the union
gains a compile-time and an AST guard so the next outcome cannot be added without a caller and
a test.
</objective>

<standing_execution_overrides>
Applies to every task in this plan. Confirmed by the user; re-stated here because an executor
reading only this file must not get any of them wrong.

1. **pnpm, never npm.** `pnpm add` / `pnpm add -D` / `pnpm dlx`. Commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`, never
   `package-lock.json`. The Supabase CLI is the Homebrew binary `/opt/homebrew/bin/supabase` —
   call it directly, not through `pnpm dlx`.
2. **`middleware.ts` does not exist — it is `proxy.ts`** (Next.js 16 rename), shipped as
   `proxy.ts` exporting `async function proxy`.
3. **Never `npx tsc` / `pnpm dlx tsc`.** The npm `tsc` package is a deprecated 2022 squatter that
   prints a notice instead of typechecking, so the gate silently passes. Use `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`.
   Task 2 of this plan depends on that gate being real.
4. **New `public` tables need explicit GRANTs.** Supabase no longer auto-exposes new entities to
   Data API roles; RLS alone returns `permission denied for table`. By design `authenticated`
   holds no INSERT and no DELETE anywhere, so a new write path is a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC,
   never a wider grant. This plan adds no table and no migration.
5. **shadcn `new-york` style no longer exists** — `components.json` records `style: "radix-nova"`.
   `shadcn add form` silently adds nothing; forms use `useActionState` + Zod. This plan adds no
   component.
6. **Never run `pnpm dev`** — it never exits and will hang the agent. Use `pnpm build`,
   `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm exec vitest run`, `pnpm lint`.
7. **`psql` is NOT installed on this machine.** The working route to the local database is
   `docker exec -i supabase_db_cena psql -U postgres -d postgres`. Any gate that would say
   `psql` uses this instead.

Additional host facts an executor cannot derive from the repo:

- Postgres **catalog tables are unreachable from any Supabase client** (`supabase/config.toml`
  exposes only `public` and `graphql_public`, and there is no Postgres driver in the
  dependencies). Use the `docker exec` route for a catalog gate, or pin the *behaviour* instead
  of the definition. Do not add a `pg` dependency and do not publish a catalog-reading RPC.
- The predicate `p.proconfig @> array['search_path=']` that appears across earlier phase-01 plan
  text is **WRONG** and returns 0 even for correctly-hardened functions — Postgres stores the
  setting as `search_path=""`. The correct literal is `array['search_path=""']`.
- **`.env.local` is gitignored and does not survive worktree removal.** Recreate it from
  `/opt/homebrew/bin/supabase status` before running any test, or the suite hard-fails in
  `tests/setup-env.ts`.
- **`lib/supabase/admin.ts` opens with `import "server-only"`, which THROWS under Vitest.**
  `actions/devices.ts` imports it, so a test that imports `@/actions/devices` must
  `vi.mock("@/lib/supabase/admin", ...)` with a factory — a `vi.mock` factory prevents the real
  module from ever being loaded, so the guard never evaluates. Do NOT delete the `server-only`
  import and do NOT add a global `server-only` alias to `vitest.config.ts`: the guard is what
  keeps the secret key out of any client-reachable import chain, and `deferred-items.md` entry

Migrations `0001`–`0007` are applied and must not be edited. `/opt/homebrew/bin/supabase db reset`

  <action>
    **Add the outcome, and refuse to reuse an existing one.**

    In `lib/device-cookie-policy.ts`, add `"registry-unreadable"` to the `owner-unlock-exit`
    `outcome` union and give it a case in the inner switch returning an empty array. Extend the
    module header: the recoverable group is now four outcomes, not three, and the new member is
    the one that says the answer never arrived at all.

    `"rotation-failed"` would produce the identical directive list, and reusing it is explicitly
    rejected. The directive list is not the only thing an outcome carries — it is also the name a
    future reader, a log line and the coverage guard in Task 2 will see. An outcome named for a
    rotation that never ran describes something that did not happen, and the next person debugging
    a fleet-wide re-enrolment would be looking at the wrong subsystem. Record that reasoning in the
    comment on the new case.

    **Stop discarding the error channel.**

    In `exitOwnerUnlock`, change the `venue_devices` read to destructure both `data` and `error`,
    naming the error binding distinctly. Insert a branch, BEFORE the existing `!device` branch,
    that fires when the error is non-null: classify as `registry-unreadable`, apply the directives
    (an empty list, so nothing is touched), sign out, and redirect to `/login`.

    The order matters and must not be flipped. `maybeSingle()` returns `data: null` alongside an
    error, so a `!device` check placed first swallows the fault exactly as it does today. Test the
    error binding first, and add a comment saying so — this is the whole defect in one line of
    control flow. The structural gate in the acceptance criteria strips comment lines before it
    checks the order, so it reads the classification call sites rather than the prose around them;
    write the comments freely, and put the outcome literal at the call site where the classification
    is actually made.

    Why sign out at all on a recoverable fault: the same reason `rotation-failed` and
    `swap-back-failed` do. This path is reached because the idle timer fired, which means the
    tablet is unattended with a full-privilege owner session on it (D-07). The session goes; the
    tablet's identity stays, so `/unlock` still offers the swap-back, the PIN pad still knows which
    device it is, and nobody has to walk to the device. State that distinction in the comment,
    because "clears nothing" is easy to misread as "does nothing".

    Also correct the comment on the `!device` branch. It currently describes that branch as the
    only terminal case in the region, written when a read fault could not be told apart from an
    absent row; it should now say what makes it terminal, which is that the query answered and the
    answer was that no live row exists.

    **Prove it against the shipped code first.**

    Create `tests/actions/device-exit-classification.test.ts`. Reuse `createCookieJar` and the
    redirect sentinel from `tests/support/server-action-harness.ts` — do not build a second cookie
    double; two doubles disagreeing is how a defect hides behind a green suite, and plan 01-11's
    jar is the one that was proven against a real defect.

    Mock `next/headers` to hand back the jar, `next/navigation` so `redirect` throws the sentinel,
    `next/cache` so `revalidatePath` is inert, `@/lib/supabase/admin` with a factory so the
    `server-only` guard is never evaluated, and `@/lib/supabase/server` with a stub client. The stub
    needs `auth.getUser`, `auth.signOut`, and a `from("venue_devices")` chain supporting
    `.select().eq().is().maybeSingle()` whose resolved value the test controls per case; a small
    chainable object whose methods return itself and whose `maybeSingle` resolves the configured
    result is enough. Mint the device cookie value with the REAL `encodeDeviceCookie` so
    `decodeDeviceCookie` runs unmodified inside the action — the codec is not the subject here, but
    a fake value would make the action take a different branch and the test would prove nothing.

    Run the file against the UNMODIFIED `actions/devices.ts` before changing it. The read-fault
    cases MUST fail by finding both cookies deleted. Record the observed failure message in the
    plan summary. The policy module has seven passing tests and could not see this defect; a test
    that has not been seen failing against it is the same kind of evidence.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Supabase network -> `exitOwnerUnlock` | An unreliable channel crosses into a function whose answers are irreversible on the device. "No answer" and "the answer is no" arrive on the same variable. |
| `IdleRelock` timer -> `exitOwnerUnlock` | A client-side timer re-enters this path unattended every three idle minutes on every owner-unlocked tablet, so any defect here is multiplied by time and by fleet size rather than being a single event. |
| caller -> `lib/device-cookie-policy.ts` | The policy is exhaustively tested and correct for every input it is given; the boundary that decides WHICH input it is given had no coverage at all. |
| type union -> caller and suite | A union member that exists in the type but in no caller and no test is surface that reports itself as designed while being unreachable and unproven. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

ASVS L1, blocking on high.

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01I-01 | Denial of Service | discarded PostgREST error in `exitOwnerUnlock` | high | mitigate | **The live finding.** `const { data: device }` drops the error channel, so a failed read is classified `device-not-active` — terminal — and both cookies are deleted. `IdleRelock` re-enters every three idle minutes, so a few minutes of Supabase interruption during service de-enrols every owner-unlocked tablet in the estate, each requiring a person on site to sign in as the owner and re-run `/enable-staff-mode`. Availability loss at exactly the moment the restaurant is busiest. Mitigation: destructure the error, classify it as its own `registry-unreadable` outcome returning no directives, and prove it by driving the real action through an injected jar in BOTH directions — fault preserves, absent row clears. |
| T-01I-02 | Tampering | reusing `rotation-failed` for the read fault | medium | mitigate | The directive lists are identical, so reuse would pass every behavioural test while naming a rotation that never ran. The next person debugging a fleet-wide re-enrolment would be sent to the wrong subsystem, and the AST coverage guard in Task 2 would report full coverage of a union that had quietly lost a distinction. Rejected explicitly; the new member carries its own name and its own comment. |
| T-01I-03 | Spoofing | a stale `cena_device_user` surviving a genuine revocation | high | mitigate | The mirror risk of over-correcting T-01I-01: if the fix preserved cookies too broadly, a genuinely revoked device would keep believing it is a tablet, which is the D-08 lost-tablet threat and strictly worse than the defect being fixed. Contained by the paired assertion — the same test file asserts that a read which SUCCEEDS and finds no live row still clears both cookies. Neither assertion is accepted without the other. |
| T-01I-04 | Elevation of Privilege | owner session left on an unattended tablet during a read fault | medium | mitigate | The recoverable branch must not become a reason to leave a full-privilege owner session resting on a device the idle timer has already judged unattended (D-07). The fix preserves the tablet's IDENTITY cookies and still signs the session out and redirects to `/login`, matching `rotation-failed` and `swap-back-failed`; asserted directly, so a future refactor that drops the sign-out turns the suite red. |
| T-01I-05 | Tampering | a silent empty directive list for an unhandled outcome | medium | mitigate | The `return []` after the inner switch makes "do nothing" the default answer for any outcome nobody wrote a case for. Correct by accident for a recoverable outcome, silently wrong for a terminal one. Task 2 replaces it with a `never`-typed assertion so the typecheck fails instead, and the failure is observed before being reverted. |
| T-01I-06 | Repudiation | union surface with no caller and no test | medium | mitigate | This is the "closed in form, defeated in effect" pattern recorded twice in `01-VERIFICATION.md`. Task 2's AST guard extracts the outcome literals from the real type and requires each to appear in a caller and in the policy suite, with the extraction itself asserted non-empty so it cannot pass vacuously. |
| T-01I-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | high | accept | This plan installs no package; `typescript` and `vitest` are already devDependencies. No `## Package Legitimacy Audit` is required because there is nothing to audit. Enforced rather than asserted: `git diff --stat pnpm-lock.yaml` must be empty in both tasks. An executor who finds themselves needing a package must stop and re-open planning. |
</threat_model>

  classify "staff members can sign in and access only the venues they belong to" into its shape
  taxonomy — the same row plan 01-10 carried forward. This plan resolves one concrete lifecycle
  edge under it (a read fault never costs a re-enrolment, and repetition of that fault accumulates
  no damage) and leaves the remaining shape questions surfaced rather than dismissed. A verifier
  that cannot confirm the wider requirement with explicit evidence must abstain to `human_needed`.
- **Probe accounting is cross-plan and lives in one place.** The ACCT-05 unclassified row above is
  row 10 of 11, and this plan's `ACCT-05 idempotency-under-fault` truth is row 1, in the
  `<probe_accounting>` table in `01-13-PLAN.md`. That table maps every probe row this plan set
  answers to the exact truth string or flagged assumption that answers it.
- **The sign-out on a recoverable fault is a judgment call, recorded as one.** Preserving the
  tablet's identity while dropping the owner session is what makes the fault free; keeping the
  owner session would leave full privilege resting on a device the idle timer has already judged
  unattended. If a future phase adds a genuine "retry in place" path, this is the branch to
  revisit — and the assertion on `auth.signOut` is what will make the change visible.
- **Both directions of the transient-failure prohibition are now live at once.** Plan 01-10 proved
  a transient failure cannot brand a laptop as the tablet; this plan proves it cannot un-brand a
  real tablet. Neither test protects the other's direction, so both must stay green together — the
  policy suite's `staff-mode-enabled` cases and this plan's read-fault cases are one pair.
</flagged_assumptions>
